title: Psalm 114: When Israel Came Out of Egypt
summary: In eight vivid verses the psalm retells the exodus and the entry into the promised land as a scene in which nature itself reacts to God. The sea flees, the Jordan turns back, and the mountains skip like rams. The poet asks them why, and then calls the whole earth to tremble before the God of Jacob, who turns rock into springs of water.
line: The exodus as a song: the sea flees, the Jordan turns back, the mountains skip like rams, and the earth trembles before the God who turns rock into springs of water.
guide: See God's great acts with fresh eyes, as if you were watching the hills jump. Where the ground of your life feels like flint, remember who he is, the one who can bring water out of stone, without demanding how he will act.

stanzas.title: Israel leaves Egypt and becomes God's dwelling
The sea, the Jordan, and the mountains react
Taunting questions: why did you flee?
Tremble before the God who makes rock into springs

verses.t: When Israel departed from Egypt, the house of Jacob from a people of foreign tongue,
Judah became God’s sanctuary, and Israel His dominion.
The sea observed and fled; the Jordan turned back;
the mountains skipped like rams, the hills like lambs.
Why was it, O sea, that you fled, O Jordan, that you turned back,
O mountains, that you skipped like rams, O hills, like lambs?
Tremble, O earth, at the presence of the Lord, at the presence of the God of Jacob,
who turned the rock into a pool, the flint into a fountain of water!
